summary: US Special Envoys Witkoff and Kushner concluded 3-hour 10-minute talks with Putin in Moscow on September 5, discussing Ukraine war cessation. Putin ordered a three-day suspension of strikes on Kyiv starting midnight September 5 to facilitate US negotiator travel. Despite the agreed ceasefire, Russian strikes continue targeting Ukrainian cities including Lubni, Khmelnytskyi, and Zhytomyr, while Ukrainian air defense engages multiple drones and loitering munitions.
key_points: Putin ordered no strikes on Kyiv for three days from midnight September 5 to facilitate US negotiator travel to Moscow and Kyiv, announced Kremlin spokesman Peskov. (Source: tass_agency/393949)
Russian Armed Forces liberated settlement of Kurtovka near Druzhkovka in DPR, confirmed by Russian Ministry of Defense. (Source: ukr_leaks_eng/33026)
Two cruise missiles struck Lubni city with confirmed impacts; preliminary reports indicate buildings were hit. (Source: mon1tor_ua/73785, mon1tor_ua/73786)
Attacks on Khmelnytskyi and Zhytomyr damaged Nova Poshta facilities; four people injured in Khmelnytskyi region including one child. (Source: UkraineNow/83907, UkraineNow/83906)
ZSU stated combat operations continue despite 'silence regime' reports, saying ceasefire cannot be unilateral or asymmetric. (Source: UkraineNow/83900)
Trump stated he spoke with Putin and believes Russia has no intention of attacking NATO territory. (Source: ukr_leaks_eng/33019)
Witkoff and Kushner departed Moscow after negotiations; expected to visit Kyiv on September 6. (Source: tass_agency/393978, UkraineNow/83903)
Multiple Banderole loitering munitions and reactive drones active over Sumy, Chernihiv, Poltava, Kyiv, and Dnipro regions. (Source: kpszsu/76701, kpszsu/76686, kpszsu/76695)

sections.executive_summary: US Special Envoys Witkoff and Kushner completed their Moscow consultations with Putin on September 5 following a 3-hour 10-minute meeting focused on Ukraine war cessation options. Putin authorized a temporary three-day suspension of strikes on Kyiv to enable safe passage of American negotiators between Moscow and Kyiv. Despite the agreed ceasefire framework, overnight strikes continued against Ukrainian cities with confirmed impacts at Lubni, Khmelnytskyi, and Zhytomyr. Russian forces simultaneously claimed territorial gains near Druzhkovka in DPR.

points: Ukrainian Armed Forces continue combat operations in full despite 'silence regime' reports, stating ceasefire cannot be unilateral or asymmetric as it would endanger military personnel lives. (Source: UkraineNow/83900)

Ukraine agreed to temporary mutual strike suspension September 5-8 to enable safe US negotiator travel to Moscow and Kyiv, with Zelensky confirming Ukraine will not attack Russia during visits. (Source: UkraineNow/83899, UkraineNow/83916)

Nova Poshta logistics facilities struck in Khmelnytskyi and Zhytomyr; Khmelnytskyi region reports four injured including a child with damage to residential apartment building and several enterprises. (Source: UkraineNow/83907, UkraineNow/83906)

Lubni city targeted with cruise missiles; mon1tor_ua reports two confirmed impacts and targeted strikes on the city; preliminary reports indicate damage to residential buildings. (Source: mon1tor_ua/73785, mon1tor_ua/73786)

Ukrainian special forces eliminated Aleksey Chernyshov, director of Putin's movement in Crimea who collected funds for Russian military, near Skvortsovo village in Simferopol district. (Source: UkraineNow/83909)

Forbes Ukraine editor reported Russia has disabled approximately the same number of Wildberries warehouses in Ukraine over two months as since February 2022, with Kiev region fires in August 2026 ten times higher than previous year. (Source: ukr_leaks_eng/33023)

Putin met with US Special Envoys Witkoff and Kushner in Kremlin for 3 hours 10 minutes; meeting described as substantive, constructive, and frank by Kremlin aide Ushakov. (Source: tass_agency/393973, tass_agency/393944)
Putin ordered no strikes on Kyiv for three days from midnight September 5, communicated through official channels, to facilitate US negotiator travel. (Source: tass_agency/393949, tass_agency/393966)

Russian Ministry of Defense confirmed Armed Forces liberated Kurtovka settlement near Druzhkovka in DPR; drone operators from Southern Group of Forces participated in liberation. (Source: ukr_leaks_eng/33026, ukr_leaks_eng/33032)

Russia continued strikes on Ukrainian cities including Khmelnytskyi where residential building was hit resulting in seven injured, and Zhytomyr targeting Nova Poshta facilities. (Source: eRadarrua/111031, UkraineNow/83906)
Putin expressed gratitude and best wishes to Trump through Witkoff and Kushner during Moscow negotiations. (Source: tass_agency/393947)
Russian aviation conducted MC-21 fully import-substituted aircraft first flight announced by Russian Ministry of Industry and Trade. (Source: tass_agency/393965)

Russian Armed Forces liberated Kurtovka settlement located near Druzhkovka in DPR, confirmed by Russian Ministry of Defense with drone operator involvement from Southern Group of Forces. (Source: ukr_leaks_eng/33026, ukr_leaks_eng/33032)
Combat operations continue on eastern front despite reports of temporary ceasefire agreement, with ZSU stating defensive operations are being executed in full. (Source: UkraineNow/83900)

Forbes Ukraine reported Russia has disabled approximately the same number of warehouses over two months of attacks as since February 2022, with August 2026 fires in Kiev region ten times higher than previous year. (Source: ukr_leaks_eng/33023)
Multiple Banderole loitering munitions active in Sumy region near Buryn heading southwest, and from Sumy toward Talalaivka in eastern Chernihiv region. (Source: kpszsu/76686, kpszsu/76689)

Two Banderole munitions passed Romen district of Sumy heading toward Chernihiv region Prilutsky district; additional two Banderole munitions in Nezhinsky district of Chernihiv heading toward Kyiv region Borshchiv district. (Source: mon1tor_ua/73788, mon1tor_ua/73795)

Banderole loitering munition heading toward Batyrin on Chernihiv region from western Sumy; additional Banderole munitions on western Sumy heading toward Chernihiv region Batyrin. (Source: kpszsu/76701)
Reactive drone heading toward Poltava from eastern Poltava region; another reactive drone between Kremenchuk and Poltava heading west. (Source: kpszsu/76698, kpszsu/76673)
Reactive drones approaching Odesa region from Black Sea toward Serhiivka and Zatoka; another drone from Black Sea heading to southern Odesa. (Source: kpszsu/76650, kpszsu/76647)
Drone activity in Odesa region near Tuzlovski limany park area heading northwest. (Source: kpszsu/76676)
Three drones on right bank and outskirts of Zaporizhzhia city; reactive drone approaching Zaporizhzhia from north. (Source: eRadarrua/111065, kpszsu/76648)
Reactive drones south of Dnipro heading northwest; reactive drones in northern Dnipropetrovsk heading west; drone heading toward Dnipro from north. (Source: kpszsu/76672, kpszsu/76692, kpszsu/76701)

Reactive drone toward Pavlohrad in Dnipropetrovsk region; drone course toward Krynychky from Zaporizhzhia direction; rocket drone in eastern Dnipropetrovsk heading north. (Source: kpszsu/76703, eRadarrua/111063)

Multiple Banderole loitering munitions targeting Kyiv region: one toward Borispol, two toward Obukhiv from east, two toward Ukrainka bypassing Obukhiv toward Vasylkiv, one toward Borshchiv district. (Source: mon1tor_ua/73796, kpszsu/76696, mon1tor_ua/73793, mon1tor_ua/73795)
Five reactive Shahed drones circling over Dnipro area; one reactive Shahed circling over Borispol district of Kyiv region. (Source: mon1tor_ua/73760)
Reactive Shahed drones targeting Kyiv region toward Irpin and Brovary; additional reactive Shahed targeting Kyiv/Brovary. (Source: mon1tor_ua/73777, mon1tor_ua/73764)

Banderole loitering munitions approaching Poltava region bypassing Pyriatyn heading southwest; another Banderole near Zmiiv in Kharkiv region heading toward Merefa. (Source: kpszsu/76695, eRadarrua/111064)

Cruise missiles struck Lubni with confirmed two impacts despite preliminary reports of being shot down; preliminary hit report indicated buildings damaged. (Source: mon1tor_ua/73785, mon1tor_ua/73786, mon1tor_ua/73782)

key_developments: Putin ordered no strikes on Kyiv for three days from midnight September 5 to enable US Special Envoys Witkoff and Kushner safe passage to Moscow and subsequently to Kyiv on September 6. (Source: tass_agency/393949, ukr_leaks_eng/33031, UkraineNow/83899)

Russian Armed Forces liberated Kurtovka settlement near Druzhkovka in DPR, with drone operators from Southern Group of Forces participating in the operation. (Source: ukr_leaks_eng/33026, ukr_leaks_eng/33032)

US Special Envoys Witkoff and Kushner completed 3-hour 10-minute meeting with Putin in Kremlin; negotiations described as substantive, constructive, and frank by Kremlin aide Ushakov. (Source: tass_agency/393973, tass_agency/393944)

Lubni city struck by cruise missiles with two confirmed impacts; preliminary reports indicated shot-down drone falling on city with damage to residential buildings. (Source: mon1tor_ua/73785, mon1tor_ua/73786, mon1tor_ua/73782)

Khmelnytskyi and Zhytomyr attacked with drones targeting Nova Poshta facilities; Khmelnytskyi region reports four injured including child with damage to apartment building and enterprises. (Source: UkraineNow/83907, UkraineNow/83906, eRadarrua/111031)
Despite temporary ceasefire agreement, ZSU states combat operations continue in full with ceasefire cannot be unilateral or asymmetric as it endangers military personnel. (Source: UkraineNow/83900)

Multiple Banderole loitering munitions and reactive drones active across northern Ukraine including Sumy, Chernihiv, Poltava regions heading toward various targets. (Source: kpszsu/76701, kpszsu/76686, kpszsu/76689, mon1tor_ua/73788)
sections.threat_assessment: The temporary three-day ceasefire arrangement appears highly fragile with continued Russian strikes on Ukrainian cities despite official suspension orders. Lubni received targeted cruise missile strikes with confirmed building impacts, while Khmelnytskyi suffered seven civilian injuries from drone attacks on residential infrastructure. The ceasefire mechanism lacks verification provisions and appears designed primarily to facilitate US diplomatic access rather than genuine conflict cessation. Russian territorial claims near Druzhkovka suggest offensive operations continue in eastern Ukraine despite diplomatic engagement.
sections.regional_response: Trump's statement that Putin has no intention of attacking NATO territory signals potential US-Russia understanding that may affect European security arrangements. NATO planners express concern about Europe's ability to sustain prolonged conflict with Russia due to right-wing party growth and reduced US support. Germany demands EU restrict tourist visas for Russians, citing contradiction with isolation strategy and normalization concerns. Czech PM Babiš noted European leaders deliberately avoided direct Putin negotiations since conflict start, potentially missing negotiation opportunities.
sections.intelligence_notes: Witkoff-Kushner Moscow visit represents highest-level direct US-Russia contact since conflict escalation, with negotiations focused on potential ceasefire frameworks. The three-day Kyiv strike suspension provides narrow window for diplomatic progress assessment. Continued overnight strikes despite ceasefire announcements indicates either authorization gaps or deliberate signaling of limited commitment. Ukrainian elimination of Chernyshov in Crimea demonstrates sustained strike capabilities against Russian officials in occupied territory.
